title: Series 47 / 47-2 water feeder: too much water, not enough, noise or burner switch
equipment: McDonnell & Miller Series 47 / 47-2 / 247 water feeder (and feeder/low-water cut-off)

options.label: Boiler is getting too much water
Boiler is not getting enough water

n2.text: Ask the tech to perform the broken union test (per the manual). Does water keep flowing into the boiler with the union broken?

options.label: No / not sure, try the blow-down valve test

r_toomuch_valve.cause: The feeder valve is not closing fully: something is holding the cartridge poppet open, or the by-pass valve is leaking.
fix: Have the tech remove and inspect the cartridge; clean or replace as necessary.
Check whether the by-pass valve is leaking; repair or replace it.
Also have the tech confirm the water supply is not above 150 psi (install a pressure reducing valve if it is).

n2b.text: Ask the tech to open the blow-down valve. Is there little or no water flow?

r_chamber.cause: The float chamber is likely clogged with sediment.
fix: Have the tech remove the bottom of the float chamber and clean sediment from the chamber, float and bellows mechanism.

r_toomuch_float.cause: The float may be full of water or the equalizing piping may be plugged.
fix: If the float has filled with water, replace it.
If the equalizing piping is plugged, clean or replace it.
Also consider system causes the manual lists: improper piping, faulty check valve in the return header, delayed condensate return, tankless coil leak, priming/foaming.

n3.text: Ask the tech to perform the broken union test. With the union broken, is water flowing from the boiler side through the piping?

r_feedline.cause: The feed line between the valve and boiler is partially plugged.
fix: Have the tech clean or replace the piping.
If supply-side flow is also poor, check the feed line to the city water supply for a blockage.

n3b.text: Ask the tech to open the blow-down valve. Is there little or no water flow?

r_notenough.cause: The cartridge poppet may not be fully opening, or the strainer is clogged. Water supply pressure may also be below boiler pressure.
fix: Have the tech remove and inspect the cartridge and the strainer; clean or replace as necessary.
If supply pressure is lower than boiler pressure, reduce boiler pressure or convert to pumped return.

r_noise.cause: Under some conditions the cartridge poppet vibrates when it is slightly open.
fix: Install a pressure reducing valve (for example a Bell & Gossett B-38) in the inlet water line ahead of the feeder valve.

r_switch.cause: The cam is worn or broken, or the linkage is not transferring float movement to the switch.
fix: If the cam is worn or broken, replace the cam assembly (CO-106/302900).
If the linkage pins are worn or broken, the valve assembly must be replaced.
Otherwise check for a damaged float, sediment in the chamber or plugged equalizing piping.

r_bellows.cause: Continuous exposure to chemicals, or water with pH above 9.0, can deteriorate the solder.
fix: Remove the source of chemicals, or replace the control with one suitable for the application.
